Subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the call earlier today. Quick written recap so we all have the same view and next steps.

Summary of pain / goals (what you told us)
- High SLA/latency requirements for customer-facing summarization and chat (95th percentile target < 300ms).
- Heavy peak concurrency during business hours; estimate ~2M tokens/day with spiky bursts around product launches.
- Cost is a top constraint: procurement gave a rough annual target of ~$120k for inference spend for this use-case.

Cost levers we discussed (high level)
- Token economics: per-token billing vs. per-request; batching reduces per-token overhead for short prompts.
- Batching & continuous batching: we can safely batch many short requests to lower effective cost without impacting median latency; we recommend small adaptive batching windows for your traffic profile.
- KV/prefix caching: for repeated system prompts and shared prefixes (e.g., product templates) we can cache and skip re-computation on warm requests — meaningful savings for high-reuse workloads.
- Quantization and model selection: using int8/4 quantized variants or a small specialized model for summaries can reduce token compute and memory footprint.
- Dedicated vs hosted: Dedicated reserved pool gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; Hosted is fastest to start but higher per-token costs.

Rough TCO framing (very coarse, ballpark)
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): $0.20–$0.40 per 1k tokens (depends on model family & quantization).
- Dedicated (1-year commit + reserved capacity): effective $60k–$140k/year depending on concurrency and model choices.
- With batching/prefix caching we typically see 20%–45% reduction in per-token compute cost for workloads like yours; exact depends on cache hit rate and request size distribution.

Attachments
- I attached a starter cost model (acme_tco_model_q1.xlsx) — it contains three scenarios (hosted, dedicated, dedicated+cache). Please review and share monthly token estimates if you want us to populate the sheet.

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm priority and the procurement/budget guardrails (is ~$120k/year a hard cap or a target?).
2) You share monthly token volume (total tokens and % of short requests) so we can populate the model.
3) Schedule a 60-min TCO deep-dive with your SRE and procurement — I’ll bring Rishi (solutions engineering) and Neha (pricing).
4) Pilot: we can offer a 30-day pilot with reduced pilot credits and a performance runbook to validate latency at 95th percentile.

Are you available for the TCO deep-dive next week (Tue/Wed preferred)? If you’d like, we can pre-populate the cost sheet — I only need the approximate monthly token volume and expected concurrency.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications/questions: 

- The $120k is a target not a hard cap; procurement will push to keep within that if possible.
- Monthly tokens: rough current estimate is 60M tokens/month for the summarization pipeline, with ~70% being short prompts (~20–80 tokens) and 30% longer context calls.
- Latency: 95th percentile today sits ~400ms (on our on-prem baseline) — we need to get down to <300ms as you noted.

On caching: if prefix caching can cut repeated prompts by half that would be huge — can you translate that to expected annual savings in the attachment?

I can do Tue next week (Mar 16) in the afternoon for the TCO deep-dive. Confirm and I’ll send calendar invites.
